# visualization.heatmaps.design_map { #fmrimod.visualization.heatmaps.design_map }

```python
design_map(
    model,
    block_separators=True,
    rotate_x_text=True,
    fill_midpoint=None,
    fill_limits=None,
    scale='column',
    palette='diverging',
    y_axis='scan',
    title=None,
    subtitle=None,
    caption=None,
    max_labels=60,
    figsize=None,
    ax=None,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Design matrix as an image, in the style of SPM (R ``design_map``).

One row per scan (time runs downward), one column per regressor.
Columns are grouped by model term under a spanner, runs are separated
by rules and labelled on the left, and the right axis marks the first
scan of each run. By default each column is divided by its maximum
absolute value (``scale="column"``) so regressors in different units
share one diverging fill with zero at the neutral midpoint. Because
that would make a near-flat regressor look healthy, a strip of bars
under the matrix shows each column's peak relative to the largest in
its term; columns below 5% of it are marked in the warning colour,
outlined, and named in the subtitle. With 12 or fewer columns each
label also gives the column's raw range.

Baseline columns are grouped by term (drift, intercept, nuisance) and
then run, with a "Run k" sub-spanner over each run's columns;
nuisance columns are veiled so the block structure dominates.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                     | Description                                                      | Default       |
|------------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| model            | (EventModel, BaselineModel or FmriModel) |                                                                  | _required_    |
| block_separators | bool                                     | Draw a rule at each run boundary.                                | `True`        |
| rotate_x_text    | bool                                     | Angle column labels when they would overlap.                     | `True`        |
| fill_midpoint    | optional                                 | Centre and limits of the fill scale (default symmetric about 0). | `None`        |
| fill_limits      | optional                                 | Centre and limits of the fill scale (default symmetric about 0). | `None`        |
| scale            | (\'column\', \'none\')                   | Divide each column by its max abs value, or plot raw values.     | `"column"`    |
| palette          | (\'diverging\', \'grey\')                | The signed palette, or white-to-ink as in SPM.                   | `"diverging"` |
| y_axis           | (\'scan\', \'time\')                     | Label the right axis by scan number or onset time (m:ss).        | `"scan"`      |
| title            | str                                      | ``None`` uses the default; ``""`` removes it.                    | `None`        |
| subtitle         | str                                      | ``None`` uses the default; ``""`` removes it.                    | `None`        |
| caption          | str                                      | ``None`` uses the default; ``""`` removes it.                    | `None`        |
| max_labels       | int                                      | Thin column labels to every k-th beyond this many.               | `60`          |
| figsize          | (float, float)                           |                                                                  | `None`        |
| ax               | matplotlib Axes                          | Draw into this axes (the colourbar is placed under it).          | `None`        |
| **kwargs         | object                                   | Passed to `matplotlib.axes.Axes.imshow`.                   | `{}`          |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description   |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------|
|        | matplotlib.figure.Figure |               |
